newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan firm's capital lifted to $9.7 ml.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan firm's capital lifted to $9.7 ml.

text.p: Morocco's leading dairy firm Centrale Laitiere has increased its capital to 83.9 million dirhams ($9.7 million) from 74.6 million dirhams, a company source said on Tuesday.
A subsidiary of Morocco's largest private conglomerate ONA Group, Centrale Laitiere said "the increased stake was devoted to French Groupe Danone ".
The decision was taken during a meeting of the firm's board of directors on October 28, 1996, it said.
ONA signed an agreement to cede 20 percent of its majority stake in Centrale Laitiere to Danone in September.

"The accord aimed at reinforcing the technological partnership with Danone and establishing the basis of development of Centrale Laitiere on the Moroccan market of fresh products," the group said at the time.
Danone holds 2.74 percent of ONA's capital under an agreement signed with the group in 1994.
Among the conglomerate's most profitable firms, Centrale Laitiere had a turnover of 2.2 billion dirhams ($255 million) in 1995.
The Moroccan firm holds respectively 55 percent of the market for milk and 75 percent of derivative dairy products.

In the last decade, the company's sales grew by an average 10 percent per year, largely better than other food industry units, including edible oil (+5.0 percent) and sugar (+3.0 percent), an analyst at Upline Securities said.
One of the 47 listed stocks on the Casablanca bourse, Centrale Laitiere was last traded at 1,390 dirhams per share, stockbrokers said.
